name: Mince jaffles
summary: Buttered bread sealed around a mildly curried savoury mince and cheese filling in a jaffle iron and toasted over coals or on the stove until crisp and golden.
about: The jaffle iron, two hinged round plates on long handles, came to South Africa from Australia after the 1940s and became part of braai and camping culture. It seals the bread at the edges so the filling stays hot inside. Savoury mince, often left over from supper, is the classic filling, and children love making their own.
steps: Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Turn the heat up, add the mince and garlic and fry for 6–8 minutes, breaking up the lumps, until browned all over.

Stir in the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute, then add the tomato paste, tomatoes, chutney, peas, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and almost dry; a wet filling makes soggy jaffles. Leave to cool for 10 minutes.
Heat the jaffle iron: on medium coals (hand at grid height for 5–6 seconds) or on a stove plate over medium heat, for 2 minutes a side.

Butter each slice of bread on one side. Lay a slice butter-side down on one plate of the open iron, spoon on about 3 heaped tablespoons of mince and a little cheese, keeping the edges clear, and top with a second slice butter-side up.

Close and clamp the iron, trim off any crust that sticks out, and toast for 3–4 minutes a side, turning once, until both sides are deep golden and crisp. Open to check; give it another minute if pale.
Turn the jaffle out onto a board, cut in half and let it stand for 2 minutes, as the filling is very hot. Repeat with the rest of the bread and filling.
prepNote: Make the mince up to 2 days ahead, or use leftover savoury mince; assemble and toast just before eating.
